I’m a senior engineer. The system always finds the corners you cut. 💻
We needed resilience before the 3x load increase. I doubled the database connection pool limit immediately, confident this decision gave us necessary headroom. 🧠
I assumed increasing the pool size solved connection contention instantly. I thought the default library settings managed resource release aggressively enough.
The moment launch traffic hit, latency jumped instantly. Not a gradual degradation, but a catastrophic spike to 1.5 seconds. The entire on-call rotation was pulled into the P0 incident. 💥
Our database CPU was flat, yet connection counts were pegged at the new maximum. We had low application errors but fatal response times. Why weren't they releasing? It made no tactical sense. This forced a humiliating full feature rollback.
The thread holding the connection was stuck waiting on an internal synchronization lock. 💀
The Moral 👇
Connection pooling manages the database resource, but synchronous application code dictates the resource's lease time.
